newsitem.title: USA: Doctors order Clinton not to speak to rest throat.
newsitem.headline: Doctors order Clinton not to speak to rest throat.

text.p: Doctors examined President Bill Clinton's throat on Wednesday and ordered him to stop talking for three to four days, the White House said, adding that Clinton already is having a hard time keeping quiet.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton's doctor, Connie Mariano, called two outside specialists to the president's residence to do a fiber-optic exam on his vocal chords. They concluded his throat was made hoarse by a combination of air travel, overuse of his vocal chords, his acid reflux condition and possibly also by his allergies.

They prescribed "complete vocal rest," McCurry said. "They would think a period of three to four days would be sufficient, but there is at least some evidence that the patient is not following doctor's orders already," he added.
McCurry said Clinton was not otherwise troubled by the condition and he set off to play golf on Wednesday afternoon.
The physicians were Dr. James Suen, Clinton's Arkansas throat doctor, and Capt. David Thompson, an ear, nose and throat specialist at Bethesda Naval Medical Centre.

McCurry said they prescribed Cisapride, a "motility agent" to control the movement of acid within his digestive system, to help ease the condition. He will take this in addition to Omeprazole, an antacid he already uses for acid reflux, a condition in which stomach acid tends to move up toward the throat.

Clinton's hoarse voice began to be noticeable about two weeks ago at the start of a 12-day trip to the Asia-Pacific region and was so bad by his return last week that his voice cracked badly during a public appearance before Thanksgiving.
White House aides said his throat, already strained by making several speeches a day during the election campaign, was further damaged by the dry air on Air Force One during the Asia trip.
"It seemed to have gotten better over Thanksgiving, when he rested a bit, but it seems to have gotten worse when he started yakking this week," McCurry said. "So the doctor is saying: No more yak."
